faqLeft.q: What engine does the Land Rover Freelander 2.5 V6 use?
faqLeft.a: The Freelander 2.5 V6 was fitted to the first-generation Freelander (L314) from 1997 to 2006. The exact engine code is not confirmed in our research — send us your registration and we'll confirm your exact engine specification before you're quoted.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Land Rover Freelander 2.5 V6 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £1,900 (based on the 4-Cyl Rebuild tier — V6 may warrant a separate tier, not confirmed). Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my Freelander 2.5 V6?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm your exact engine code and specification before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild Freelander 2.5 V6 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We rebuild Freelander 2.5 V6 engines to the same high standard as every other engine we work on.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Freelander 2.5 V6 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Freelander 2.5 V6 if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does a Freelander 2.5 V6 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most Freelander owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
